in_hebrew.name: גאיוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: גאיוס הוא שם שמקורו ברומי, אך הוא מופיע גם בברית החדשה. הוא נגזר מהמילה הרומית 'גאוס', שפירושה שמחה או ששון. השם גאיוס היה נפוץ ברומי ובאימפריה הרומית, והוא הועבר גם לנצרות הקדומה. במסורת הנוצרית, גאיוס הוא שם של קדוש וגם של כמה דמויות מקראיות.

in_greek.name: Γαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: Γαῖος είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του ρωμαϊκού ονόματος Gaius. Προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'gaudere', που σημαίνει να χαίρομαι. Στο Καινόν Διαθήκη, ο Γαῖος αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους υποστηρικτές του Παύλου. Ο Γαῖος είναι ένα όνομα που συμβολίζει τη χαρά και την ευφροσύνη, και ήταν δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Ελλάδα και Ρώμη.

in_latin.name: Gaius
in_latin.long_meaning: Gaius est nomen Romanum, quod gaudium vel laetitiam significat. Nomen Gaius a verbo 'gaudere' derivatur, quod est origine Latina. In Ecclesia primitiva, Gaius fuit nomen sancti et aliorum virorum illustrium. Gaius est nomen, quod vitam et gaudium repraesentat.

in_english.name: Gaius
in_english.long_meaning: Gaius is a Christian name derived from the Latin word 'gaudere', meaning to rejoice. It was a common Roman name, adopted by early Christians. In the New Testament, Gaius is mentioned as a supporter of St. Paul. The name symbolizes joy, happiness, and spiritual fulfillment. Gaius is associated with several saints and biblical figures, reflecting its significance in Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gaius held significant importance in the ancient Roman culture. It was a common Roman name worn by patricians, or noblemen. Gaius Julius Caesar, a renowned Roman general, statesman, and philosopher under the Roman Republic, who played a decisive role in the events that led to the transition of the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire, bore this name. The cultural influence of the name Gaius can also be traced in the New Testament, where several early Christian figures, including St. Gaius of Corinth, bore this name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Gaius holds a deeper spiritual significance. St. Gaius of Corinth was an early Christian bishop and a teacher of the faith. He is best known for his two letters in the New Testament, which are part of the Pauline Epistles. In his letters, St. Gaius offers guidance and encouragement to the Christian communities of Corinth and marks the importance of love and living a life worthy of the Gospel. The name Gaius, which means 'glad' or 'happy', becomes a reminder to its bearer to joyously live the Christian faith and spread the love and hope of the Gospel.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gaius in early Christianity symbolizes generosity and hospitality. Derived from the Latin name Gaius, it represents the open door of a friend's home and the warm welcome extended to travelers and strangers in need. This name embodies the spirit of Christian fellowship and love, encouraging community and unity among believers.

biblical_reference.note: Gaius is mentioned as a Christian in Corinth and a supporter of Paul.

historical_references.reference: Gaius was a Roman senator and consul during the late 1st century AD, who was also known as Gaius Calpurnius Piso. He was a patron of the poet Martial and was implicated in the conspiracy of Piso's son, Gaius Calpurnius Piso the Younger, against Emperor Nero in AD 65.
historical_references.context: Roman senator and consul, patron of poet Martial, implicated in conspiracy against Emperor Nero

historical_references.reference: Gaius Aurelianus was a Roman general who served under Emperor Valens during the late 4th century AD. He is most famous for his military campaigns against the Visigoths and Huns, which led to the establishment of the militarized frontier known as the Limes Transalutanus.
historical_references.context: Roman general, military campaigns against Visigoths and Huns, established Limes Transalutanus
